title: Comparison of the Effectiveness of Digital-Based and Manual Psychospiritual Therapies on Physical and Psychological Outcomes Among Breast Cancer Patients: A Scoping Review
content: Background and Aim: Breast cancer remains the most prevalent malignancy among women worldwide and is associated with significant physical and psychological burdens, including fatigue, anxiety, depression, and fear of recurrence. Psychospiritual interventions have emerged as complementary approaches to address these challenges. With the expansion of digital health, such interventions are delivered through both manual and digital modalities, yet comparative evidence remains limited. This scoping review aims to map and compare the effectiveness of digital and manual psychospiritual interventions among breast cancer patients. Methods and Materials: This scoping review followed PRISMA-ScR guidelines. Literature searches were conducted in PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, and CINAHL for studies published between 2016 and 2026. Eligible studies involved adult breast cancer patients receiving digital or manual psychospiritual interventions with reported physical and/or psychological outcomes. Data were synthesized narratively. Results: Twenty studies were included. Manual interventions (e.g., mindfulness, cognitive behavioral therapy, spiritual therapy) showed consistent improvements in psychological outcomes (anxiety, depression, quality of life) and physical outcomes (fatigue). Digital interventions (e.g., telehealth, web-based programs) also demonstrated positive effects, particularly for psychological outcomes, though with greater variability. Both modalities showed comparable effectiveness in some domains. Conclusion: Both approaches are effective with context-dependent advantages. Manual interventions provide more consistent benefits, while digital modalities enhance accessibility. Hybrid models may optimize psychospiritual care in oncology.
